items: T5 Judgment — Establish prior art by affected flow.py/integrate.py paths across merged history and closed/rejected work before approving novelty — the available git history contains only one synthetic base commit, no remotes, and no closed/rejected-work evidence; the brief names predecessors but cannot settle this check (review-prior-art.log:1; brief.md:18).

**A stranded partner hides a real overlap.** `template/src/pdca_harness/integrate.py:1855-1857` marks a partner "stranded" when its head does not merge onto the new base. `template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:1566-1568` then puts each partner in exactly one bucket, so a stranded partner never gets the `Conflicts with` proposal. Failing case (probe A): `A` edits `shared.txt` and `a.txt`; after wave 0's fold, `main` edits `a.txt`; `Y` (wave 1, built on the moved main) edits `shared.txt`. The output is `issue_Y held … issue_A's branch … does not merge cleanly onto origin/main itself … (conflicts in a.txt, shared.txt) … rebuild issue_A's branch on the new origin/main`, and nothing is said to Y's owner. After A rebuilds, Y still clashes with A on `shared.txt` (both add the file), so the advice takes two re-runs and wrongly suggests Y's change is not involved. The patch implements the brief's discriminator ("partner's head does not merge onto the base alone → fix aimed at the partner") faithfully, so this needs a human call on the rule. One trial-based fix would be to also try `base + partner (its side winning, _merge_over) + head` and give both steps when that still conflicts.

**A stranded line bundle holds every later bundle, after building it.** In probes A and C, once `main` moves in a file a line bundle touched, every bundle built on the moved main carries that change and clashes with the line bundle in that file. Each one is fully built, then held, each naming `issue_A`. Probe C is case (3)'s shape with a plain `Depends on` chain (`S` depends on `R`, `T` depends on `S`). `S`, which only adds `s.txt`, is held "for a.txt", `T` is skipped, and the result is `holds={'S','W': 'conflict'}`, exit 1. Case (3)'s test meets "an unrelated bundle completes" only because `S` is `Stacks on: R` (`template/tests/test_flow_cross_wave_fold_holds.py:308`), which cuts it from the old line without the moved main. Before the patch the run stopped once, with one message. Now it spends a build on every later bundle and folds none of them. Decision 2 may not have meant this. One option is to treat a stranded line bundle as a failure of the shared line (stop, or hold later waves before building).

`template/src/pdca_harness/integrate.py:1847-1850`: the "together" fallback names every bundle on the line except the ones `head` already holds. That means every earlier wave's bundles plus the carried finished ids, not only the same-wave `kept` that `_held_by` names (`:1798`). On a long line one combined clash can produce a `Conflicts with:` proposal listing many unrelated bundles (`flow.py:1589-1593`). No smaller set is searched for. Case (4) only has three bundles on the line, so the test cannot show this. Is "name all of them" acceptable at this scale, or should the set be narrowed (e.g. drop each partner whose removal still leaves the trial conflicting)?

**The tracker record is missing, so the problem statement can't be checked against it.** The cwd has only `brief.md` and `dependency-state.json`. There is no `notes.json` and no `sources/`. The brief rests on "the human's decisions at the #725 re-plan (2026-10-17, decisions 2-4)" and on `results/issue_725/iteration-v1/SUMMARY.md` §6/§9. That file is not in the bundle, and Glob finds no `results/issue_725/**` under `$PDCA_TARGET` either. Three things depend on that record: (a) the flip of a test that #674 deliberately named "still stops the run", (b) exit 1 rather than 3, and (c) "Bases are not pinned to the run's start". None of the three can be traced to the thread. The human should confirm the decisions are recorded where Check can read them.

**Prerequisite #738 is PLANNED, but the brief treats it as accepted.** `dependency-state.json`: `"738": {"exists": true, "state": "PLANNED"}`. The brief says: "Do builds and the gate verifies on … `pdca-integration/main-r547f8028520f` with #738's accepted work folded on top". The Falsifiability line adds "Case (3) needs #738 on the base (otherwise the run stops earlier…)". Until #738 is accepted and folded, there is no verify base that can turn case (3) green. Both bundles also edit the same `_runnable`/held-set call (`flow.py:2497-2502` on the target). The bundle will strand at Do or Check unless #738 lands first. Otherwise case (3) needs an explicit fallback.
**The line anchors don't match the target, and the brief contradicts itself on one of them.** The target's HEAD is `2ff8f3b`, not `75a886e`. Where things are on the target:

**The path-ownership rule contradicts the case it must keep as a stop.** The rule: "every conflicting path is owned by a bundle branch already on the line". In `test_a_conflict_only_with_a_base_taken_in_mid_wave_still_stops_the_run` (`test_flow_same_wave_conflict.py:378-409`), 22 conflicts in `shared.txt`. 20 is on the line and also changes `shared.txt` (`:380`), so 20 "owns" that path. A literal per-path rule would therefore hold 22 and blame 20. The test comment at `:401-403` says exactly that must not happen: "Holding it would blame 20 and propose a wrong `Conflicts with: 20`". #674 decides by trial merges, not by path ownership (`_held_by`, `integrate.py:1279-1285`). The rule should be restated as a trial-merge test, e.g. `_clash` returning `"batch"`. As written, Do may implement it by paths and flip case (5).

**"Reuse `_partners`" can't produce the "together" case (4) as specified.** `_partners` (`integrate.py:1349-1360`) names a bundle only when `head` conflicts with `base + that bundle alone` (`at != 1: continue`). If the clash happens only with several bundles together, it returns `{}`. `_clash` then falls through to `"line"`/`"moved"`/`"off"` (`:1320-1328`), and those name no bundle. The "all of kept" fallback the brief cites exists only in `_held_by` (`:1285`). So "Reuse `_clash` / `_partners` rather than adding a second classifier" and case (4) pull in opposite directions. The brief should say which function gets the "together" fallback, and that changing `_clash`'s contract also changes its #694 caller, the pre-wave carry (`_clash` docstring, `:1291-1295`).

**The flipped test (5) doesn't fit the brief's own wording rule.** The target `:351-366`: 21 has `Depends on: 10` (`:357`) and is cut from `origin/main` (`:359`), so it clashes with 10 on the line. The brief flips it to "21 held and named with `issue_10`". But 10 is 21's own prerequisite, and #674's hold proposes a `Conflicts with` partner. Two things are unclear: whether 21 is told to declare `Conflicts with: 10` against its own dependency, and whether 21 is told to rebuild on 10's line. Case (3) forbids "blame W / tell W's owner to update its branch" for a bundle cut from main. 21 is in exactly that position, but the brief gives no expected wording for it. Specify the stderr text for this flip, or the reviewer can't tell right from wrong.
**The scope holds more than one fix.** The single "one logical fix" covers five things:

**"The exit code" isn't something `flow._drive_and_act` returns.** It returns `results` and fills `holds` (`flow.py:2694-2698`). The exit code comes from `cli._results_rc(results, holds=…)` (`cli.py:701-731`). Holds alone give 3, and a non-terminal bundle such as a PLANNED dependent gives 1. The criterion should say the tests compute the code through `cli._results_rc`, and should give the expected code for each case. Case (1)'s U is COMPLETE, but whether Y's dependents stay PLANNED (rc 1) or Y is the only one held (rc 3) isn't stated per case.

`template/src/pdca_harness/integrate.py:1854-1856` → `template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:1571-1580`: the "stranded" test asks only whether the partner's own change conflicts with `<remote>/main` *somewhere*. It never checks that this conflict has anything to do with the clash that held the bundle. Failing shape: the base moved and now conflicts with partner `A` in `x.txt`, while `Y` (built on the new base) clashes with `A` only because both add `shared.txt`. `A` is called stranded, so `Y`'s line says only "rebuild issue_A's branch on the new origin/main". That rebuild fixes `x.txt` but leaves the `shared.txt` clash, so `Y` is held again on the next run, and no `Conflicts with` is proposed. The brief words the rule exactly this way ("`_trial(base, [partner head])` conflicts"), so this is a gap in the rule, not a departure from it. One possible tightening, still decided by trial merges: count a partner as stranded only when the files of its own conflict with the base overlap the held bundle's conflict `paths`. Otherwise treat it as an `other` partner. Untested either way.

T5 Judgment — Confirm merged history and closed/rejected prior work by both affected production paths — the required path-based investigation found only the synthetic base commit and no remote; the brief's named precedents cannot establish the closed-work check (`review-evidence/prior-art.log:1`, `review-evidence/prior-art.log:5`).

The fix is bigger than the brief planned. The brief says to reuse `_clash` / `_partners`, and that "the only new trial is the 'together' fallback, mirrored from `_held_by`". The patch adds about 150 lines of new trial logic: `_held_on_line` (`template/src/pdca_harness/integrate.py:1804`) with its own stranded / rebuild trials (`:1873-1883`), `_holds_newer` (`:1891`), and `_together` (`:1901`). `_together` does a per-file leave-one-out search plus a walk over the bundles that carry a partner's change (`:1943-1952`), which `_held_by` (`:1797-1801`) does not do. Each piece answers a finding from rounds 1 and 2, and `_clash` itself is unchanged, as the brief asked. Still, this is now a second classifier with its own rules next to `_clash`, which is what the iteration-v1 review objected to. A human should decide whether this much new logic is wanted, or whether some of the edge cases (joint clashes in several files, stranded partners stacked on other bundles) should stop the run instead.
